One day, we were playing with some of these toys in the basement.  There was a shiny red devil figurine with a bead-chain loop atop its head.  I believe it was a bonus part of a Bratz set. One day, we were playing with some of these toys in the basement.  There was a shiny red devil figurine with a bead-chain loop atop its head.  I believe it was a bonus part of a Bratz set.  I'm not sure what happened prior to this event that set me off, whether she had been very rude or frustrating or simply the way she was interacting with the others, but we were all to go upstairs and I was the last to leave the room.</p><p><br></p><p>I decided that I wanted this toy.  I had never stolen before, nor had I ever been tempted.  But I saw that it was small, and that it would be easily hidden, and that I had opportunity.  I tucked it away secretly and followed upstairs behind them.</p><p><br></p><p>I remember that on that day, I felt a thrill inside me: I was worried I would be caught, that the bump in my pocket would show or it would be seen when I put it in my bag.  But no one did, and there was a sort of giddiness with getting away with it when my mother collected me and I went home.  </p><p><br></p><p>The next challenge was to secret it away at home.  I desperately did not want my mother to ask where I had gotten it, for fear she would put everything together.  My schoolbag did not live in my bedroom; it lived in the living room, for easy access and to be dealt with, which meant I would need to secretly move this toy from my bag to my room without her noticing I did it.  I was worried she would turn from the other room at just the wrong moment, but nothing of the sort happened.  I got into my room, and put my prize on the little shelf inside my wardrobe.  I often kept things in here to look at and play with as there was a mirror on the inside: I would do dress-up here, and the canopies from my bed could make it into a nice secret zone.  I would be able to admire it and play with it in secret without trouble here.</p><p><br></p><p>Over the next few days, I saw it every time I got changed.  It caught my attention.  The shine of the red was unavoidable. The thrill of successfully hiding it never quite got rid of the worry of it being seen and my being caught.  Eventually, after those few days, that worry also began to turn into guilt.  Every time I saw the figure that guilt would spike.  I had stolen this.  This did not belong to me.  This was someone else's, and I should not have taken it.  Even if that person was unkind, rude, boorish, and all manner of things, I had debased myself beyond her level, I felt, and I didn't know what to do.</p><p><br></p><p>I had managed to get it home unseen.  But how on Earth would I ever return it?  I wanted to.  The desire within me to do so was incredible.  I did not want this reminder of misdeeds.  I wanted to make it right.  But I did not want it to be known.  The other girl had not said anything about noticing it being missing, and I did not want to present it to show what I had done.  I felt I needed to give it back as secretly as I had taken it, with no one any the wiser.</p><p><br></p><p>But there was no easy way to do that.  Being unseen in the playroom to remove something I shouldn't have from my pockets? Unlikely. I risked too much being discovered and I would not have my reputation smeared.</p><p><br></p><p>So it sat at home, and I worried.  It permeated my thoughts.  How to return it?  What could I do?  Guilt ate at me, until finally, inspiration struck: I could slip it into the girl's things at school.</p><p><br></p><p>As we were a year apart, we were in different grades, with different classes. I was worried she would turn from the other room at just the wrong moment, but nothing of the sort happened.  I got into my room, and put my prize on the little shelf inside my wardrobe.  I often kept things in here to look at and play with as there was a mirror on the inside: I would do dress-up here, and the canopies from my bed could make it into a nice secret zone. I would be able to admire it and play with it in secret without trouble here.</p><p><br></p><p>Over the next few days, I saw it every time I got changed.  It caught my attention.  The shine of the red was unavoidable. The thrill of successfully hiding it never quite got rid of the worry of it being seen and my being caught.  Eventually, after those few days, that worry also began to turn into guilt.  Every time I saw the figure that guilt would spike.  I had stolen this.  This did not belong to me.  This was someone else's, and I should not have taken it. I was worried she would turn from the other room at just the wrong moment, but nothing of the sort happened.  I got into my room, and put my prize on the little shelf inside my wardrobe.  I often kept things in here to look at and play with as there was a mirror on the inside: I would do dress-up here, and the canopies from my bed could make it into a nice secret zone.  I would be able to admire it and play with it in secret without trouble here.</p><p><br></p><p>Over the next few days, I saw it every time I got changed.  It caught my attention.  The shine of the red was unavoidable. The thrill of successfully hiding it never quite got rid of the worry of it being seen and my being caught.  Eventually, after those few days, that worry also began to turn into guilt.  Every time I saw the figure that guilt would spike.  I had stolen this.  This did not belong to me.  This was someone else's, and I should not have taken it.  Even if that person was unkind, rude, boorish, and all manner of things, I had debased myself beyond her level, I felt, and I didn't know what to do.</p><p><br></p><p>I had managed to get it home unseen. But I did not want it to be known.  The other girl had not said anything about noticing it being missing, and I did not want to present it to show what I had done.  I felt I needed to give it back as secretly as I had taken it, with no one any the wiser.</p><p><br></p><p>But there was no easy way to do that. I'm not sure what happened prior to this event that set me off, whether she had been very rude or frustrating or simply the way she was interacting with the others, but we were all to go upstairs and I was the last to leave the room.</p><p><br></p><p>I decided that I wanted this toy.  I had never stolen before, nor had I ever been tempted.  But I saw that it was small, and that it would be easily hidden, and that I had opportunity.  I tucked it away secretly and followed upstairs behind them.</p><p><br></p><p>I remember that on that day, I felt a thrill inside me: I was worried I would be caught, that the bump in my pocket would show or it would be seen when I put it in my bag. I was worried she would turn from the other room at just the wrong moment, but nothing of the sort happened.  I got into my room, and put my prize on the little shelf inside my wardrobe.  I often kept things in here to look at and play with as there was a mirror on the inside: I would do dress-up here, and the canopies from my bed could make it into a nice secret zone.  I would be able to admire it and play with it in secret without trouble here.</p><p><br></p><p>Over the next few days, I saw it every time I got changed.  It caught my attention.  The shine of the red was unavoidable. The thrill of successfully hiding it never quite got rid of the worry of it being seen and my being caught.  Eventually, after those few days, that worry also began to turn into guilt.  Every time I saw the figure that guilt would spike.  I had stolen this.  This did not belong to me.  This was someone else's, and I should not have taken it.  Even if that person was unkind, rude, boorish, and all manner of things, I had debased myself beyond her level, I felt, and I didn't know what to do.</p><p><br></p><p>I had managed to get it home unseen. I was worried she would turn from the other room at just the wrong moment, but nothing of the sort happened.  I got into my room, and put my prize on the little shelf inside my wardrobe.  I often kept things in here to look at and play with as there was a mirror on the inside: I would do dress-up here, and the canopies from my bed could make it into a nice secret zone.  I would be able to admire it and play with it in secret without trouble here.</p><p><br></p><p>Over the next few days, I saw it every time I got changed.  It caught my attention.  The shine of the red was unavoidable. The thrill of successfully hiding it never quite got rid of the worry of it being seen and my being caught.  Eventually, after those few days, that worry also began to turn into guilt.  Every time I saw the figure that guilt would spike.  I had stolen this.  This did not belong to me.  This was someone else's, and I should not have taken it.  Even if that person was unkind, rude, boorish, and all manner of things, I had debased myself beyond her level, I felt, and I didn't know what to do.</p><p><br></p><p>I had managed to get it home unseen.  But how on Earth would I ever return it?  I wanted to.  The desire within me to do so was incredible.  I did not want this reminder of misdeeds.  I wanted to make it right.  But I did not want it to be known.  The other girl had not said anything about noticing it being missing, and I did not want to present it to show what I had done.  I felt I needed to give it back as secretly as I had taken it, with no one any the wiser.</p><p><br></p><p>But there was no easy way to do that.  Being unseen in the playroom to remove something I shouldn't have from my pockets? Unlikely.  It was an unfinished basement with stud walls and mirrors in multiple places due to a bathroom they were slowly installing.  There were too many ways to be seen, and it was very unlikely I'd be the only person or last person down there again as that was unusual to begin with.  And that would rely on my having it on my person.  Dangerous.  No, I felt; this was too risky.  I could not do so.  I risked too much being discovered and I would not have my reputation smeared.</p><p><br></p><p>So it sat at home, and I worried.  It permeated my thoughts.  How to return it?  What could I do?  Guilt ate at me, until finally, inspiration struck: I could slip it into the girl's things at school.</p><p><br></p><p>As we were a year apart, we were in different grades, with different classes.  I lived in Canada where we must change our shoes to indoor shoes on entering the building, and replace them with our outdoor shoes on exit.  We spent all day in our classrooms except for gym class.  Our coats and bags were kept in the hallways and mudrooms on rows of hooks with our shoes set beneath them.  And this girl's classes' hooks were on the route my class walked to get to and from our class to the gym.</p><p><br></p><p>So.  Having decided what I could do, I once again secreted my ill-gotten gains upon my person.  I snuck it with me to school, and I believe I tucked it in my desk so I would not miss my opportunity. One day, we were playing with some of these toys in the basement.  There was a shiny red devil figurine with a bead-chain loop atop its head.  I believe it was a bonus part of a Bratz set.  I'm not sure what happened prior to this event that set me off, whether she had been very rude or frustrating or simply the way she was interacting with the others, but we were all to go upstairs and I was the last to leave the room.</p><p><br></p><p>I decided that I wanted this toy.  I had never stolen before, nor had I ever been tempted.  But I saw that it was small, and that it would be easily hidden, and that I had opportunity.  I tucked it away secretly and followed upstairs behind them.</p><p><br></p><p>I remember that on that day, I felt a thrill inside me: I was worried I would be caught, that the bump in my pocket would show or it would be seen when I put it in my bag.  But no one did, and there was a sort of giddiness with getting away with it when my mother collected me and I went home.  </p><p><br></p><p>The next challenge was to secret it away at home.  I desperately did not want my mother to ask where I had gotten it, for fear she would put everything together.  My schoolbag did not live in my bedroom; it lived in the living room, for easy access and to be dealt with, which meant I would need to secretly move this toy from my bag to my room without her noticing I did it.  I was worried she would turn from the other room at just the wrong moment, but nothing of the sort happened.  I got into my room, and put my prize on the little shelf inside my wardrobe.  I often kept things in here to look at and play with as there was a mirror on the inside: I would do dress-up here, and the canopies from my bed could make it into a nice secret zone.  I would be able to admire it and play with it in secret without trouble here.</p><p><br></p><p>Over the next few days, I saw it every time I got changed.  It caught my attention.  The shine of the red was unavoidable. The thrill of successfully hiding it never quite got rid of the worry of it being seen and my being caught.  Eventually, after those few days, that worry also began to turn into guilt.  Every time I saw the figure that guilt would spike.  I had stolen this.  This did not belong to me.  This was someone else's, and I should not have taken it.  Even if that person was unkind, rude, boorish, and all manner of things, I had debased myself beyond her level, I felt, and I didn't know what to do.</p><p><br></p><p>I had managed to get it home unseen. I felt I needed to give it back as secretly as I had taken it, with no one any the wiser.</p><p><br></p><p>But there was no easy way to do that. One day, we were playing with some of these toys in the basement.  There was a shiny red devil figurine with a bead-chain loop atop its head.  I believe it was a bonus part of a Bratz set.  I'm not sure what happened prior to this event that set me off, whether she had been very rude or frustrating or simply the way she was interacting with the others, but we were all to go upstairs and I was the last to leave the room.</p><p><br></p><p>I decided that I wanted this toy.  I had never stolen before, nor had I ever been tempted.  But I saw that it was small, and that it would be easily hidden, and that I had opportunity.  I tucked it away secretly and followed upstairs behind them.</p><p><br></p><p>I remember that on that day, I felt a thrill inside me: I was worried I would be caught, that the bump in my pocket would show or it would be seen when I put it in my bag.  But no one did, and there was a sort of giddiness with getting away with it when my mother collected me and I went home.  </p><p><br></p><p>The next challenge was to secret it away at home.  I desperately did not want my mother to ask where I had gotten it, for fear she would put everything together.  My schoolbag did not live in my bedroom; it lived in the living room, for easy access and to be dealt with, which meant I would need to secretly move this toy from my bag to my room without her noticing I did it.  I was worried she would turn from the other room at just the wrong moment, but nothing of the sort happened.  I got into my room, and put my prize on the little shelf inside my wardrobe.  I often kept things in here to look at and play with as there was a mirror on the inside: I would do dress-up here, and the canopies from my bed could make it into a nice secret zone.  I would be able to admire it and play with it in secret without trouble here.</p><p><br></p><p>Over the next few days, I saw it every time I got changed.  It caught my attention.  The shine of the red was unavoidable. The thrill of successfully hiding it never quite got rid of the worry of it being seen and my being caught.  Eventually, after those few days, that worry also began to turn into guilt.  Every time I saw the figure that guilt would spike.  I had stolen this.  This did not belong to me.  This was someone else's, and I should not have taken it.  Even if that person was unkind, rude, boorish, and all manner of things, I had debased myself beyond her level, I felt, and I didn't know what to do.</p><p><br></p><p>I had managed to get it home unseen.  But how on Earth would I ever return it?  I wanted to.  The desire within me to do so was incredible.  I did not want this reminder of misdeeds.  I wanted to make it right.  But I did not want it to be known.  The other girl had not said anything about noticing it being missing, and I did not want to present it to show what I had done.  I felt I needed to give it back as secretly as I had taken it, with no one any the wiser.</p><p><br></p><p>But there was no easy way to do that.  Being unseen in the playroom to remove something I shouldn't have from my pockets? Unlikely.  It was an unfinished basement with stud walls and mirrors in multiple places due to a bathroom they were slowly installing.  There were too many ways to be seen, and it was very unlikely I'd be the only person or last person down there again as that was unusual to begin with. I risked too much being discovered and I would not have my reputation smeared.</p><p><br></p><p>So it sat at home, and I worried.  It permeated my thoughts.  How to return it?  What could I do?  Guilt ate at me, until finally, inspiration struck: I could slip it into the girl's things at school.</p><p><br></p><p>As we were a year apart, we were in different grades, with different classes.  I lived in Canada where we must change our shoes to indoor shoes on entering the building, and replace them with our outdoor shoes on exit.  We spent all day in our classrooms except for gym class.  Our coats and bags were kept in the hallways and mudrooms on rows of hooks with our shoes set beneath them.  And this girl's classes' hooks were on the route my class walked to get to and from our class to the gym.</p><p><br></p><p>So. Even if that person was unkind, rude, boorish, and all manner of things, I had debased myself beyond her level, I felt, and I didn't know what to do.</p><p><br></p><p>I had managed to get it home unseen.  But how on Earth would I ever return it?  I wanted to.  The desire within me to do so was incredible.  I did not want this reminder of misdeeds.  I wanted to make it right.  But I did not want it to be known.  The other girl had not said anything about noticing it being missing, and I did not want to present it to show what I had done.  I felt I needed to give it back as secretly as I had taken it, with no one any the wiser.</p><p><br></p><p>But there was no easy way to do that. I risked too much being discovered and I would not have my reputation smeared.</p><p><br></p><p>So it sat at home, and I worried.  It permeated my thoughts.  How to return it?  What could I do? Our coats and bags were kept in the hallways and mudrooms on rows of hooks with our shoes set beneath them.  And this girl's classes' hooks were on the route my class walked to get to and from our class to the gym.</p><p><br></p><p>So. When it was time to go to the gym class I slipped it into my pocket--and, as we passed by her shoes, I would palm it and dropped it into one of her flats just so.  The goal was for it to be hidden by the toe cap so she would not see it, but feel it when she put her shoe on, and simply wonder where it came from and why with no way to tie it to me.  I would need to do it nonchalantly, without leaning much or being noticed to have dropped it by my peers with whom I was walking.</p><p><br></p><p>Tricky.
